claims.explanation: Didanosine is a nucleoside analog that requires intracellular phosphorylation and is detoxified by purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP); its active metabolite dideoxyadenosine triphosphate competes with endogenous purines and inhibits mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma, causing chain termination and mitochondrial toxicity. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on purine salvage and mitochondrial DNA replication, so tumors with high PNP expression (rapid drug inactivation) are protected, while loss of PNP or high nucleoside transporter/kinase activity sensitizes. The observed enrichment of KRAS/PIK3CA/BRAF mutations and ARID1A loss in sensitive lines suggests these pathways increase purine demand and mitochondrial dependence, whereas PNP-high or low-proliferation lineages survive.

features.basis: PNP is the annotated didanosine target and inactivates the drug by phosphorolysis; high expression reduces active metabolite
KRAS-mutant lines (SW480, LU99, NCIH1792, GP2D) are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with increased purine demand and mitochondrial dependence
BRAF-mutant lines (AM38, CAL12T, RPMI7951, RL952) are enriched among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK-driven purine demand
PIK3CA-mutant lines (MKN1, LU99, KYSE70, GP2D) are enriched among sensitive lines, linking PI3K signaling to nucleotide synthesis
ARID1A loss appears in several sensitive lines (COLO792, CCLFPEDS0003T, RL952, KYSE70, GP2D) and may impair DNA repair, increasing dependence on nucleotide pools
TP53 mutation is nearly universal in both groups, so it is not selective; however, TP53 wild-type status may enhance sensitivity to DNA damage and is not enriched in resistant lines
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lines (SNU899, MHHES1, RD, BHY, PLCPRF5, VMCUB1, KELLY) and may reduce proliferation/dependence on mitochondrial metabolism
PTEN mutation appears in resistant lines (8MGBA, SF295, OVK18) and may reduce PI3K-driven purine synthesis
ATM mutation in sensitive lines (CCLFPEDS0003T, RL952) may impair DNA damage response and increase reliance on nucleotide pools
SF3B1 mutation in sensitive lines (CAL12T, HEPG2, NCIH1703) may alter splicing of nucleotide metabolism genes
NF1 mutation in sensitive lines (COLO792, GP2D) may activate RAS/MAPK and increase purine demand
EGFR mutation in sensitive lines (RL952, NCIH1650, KYSE70) may drive proliferation and nucleotide demand
